body:
Adds an errata entry dated 2026-11-04 and a one-line notice on /compliance and /compliance/nist-ai-rmf, both linking to /errata. No rule file changes.

What the entry records, each counted on main at 7add9e397:
- The NIST AI RMF generator's reference table gave MG.2.3 the meaning of MG.2.4, GV.1.2 the meaning of GV.2.1 and MP.5.2 the meaning of MG.1.3. 556 mappings cite MG.2.3 (550 in effective rules) and 25 cite GV.1.2; none cite MP.5.2.
- 101 rule files say deploying the rule "satisfies" an EU AI Act article, which docs/COMPLIANCE-COVERAGE-POLICY.md forbids.
- 25 files cite a "mandatory Article 9 risk category"; 50 apply Article 10 to run-time data.
- 26 of 43 model-abuse rules map to OWASP ASI08 and LLM02.

Detection is not affected: the engine never reads the compliance or references blocks.

Checked: website typecheck and a full static build; the entry renders on /en/errata and /zh/errata and the notice on both compliance pages in both languages.

The fixes: #779 (wording), #781 (NIST, stacked on #779), #782 (OWASP, stacked on #781). The Article 9 and Article 10 wording is not fixed by any of them yet.
title: docs(errata): framework mappings are known to be wrong and are being redone
head: fix/mapping-errata
